title: General-purpose computing environment
summary: A compiler, transactional data store and dynamic route planner built on the Brainfuck (BF) programming language.
commitConvention: The starting commit establishes the experiment. The ending commit is the exact implementation/evidence candidate verified in a clean public clone and Linux CI. Subsequent commits seal metadata and append the deployment receipt without changing executable code. The build-001 tag identifies final closure; the Site receipt records its exact deployed source commit.
architecture: Thread is a Forth-inspired interactive compiler and threaded runtime generated into pure eight-command Brainfuck with 16-bit cells. Native Thread programs implement transactional indexed storage and Dispatch. Generic JS/Wasm executors provide instruction execution and byte I/O.
majorDecisions: Native compiler and reusable definitions, with no host compiler for guest source
Separate bounded data/return/control stacks, code, dictionary, heap and store
Native hash dictionary and open-addressed store
Generic Wasm acceleration with literal differential references
Whole-machine continuation images with atomic host file saves
Dynamic public browser execution using the identical artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Compile and execute new reusable programs entirely inside the BF kernel
Structured control flow, recursion, variables, bounded memory and recoverable diagnostics
Persistent abstraction supports updates, transactions, capacity refusal and integrity checks
Save real programs, data and paused continuation; resume across process lifetimes
Dynamic non-trivial route application responds to changed input
Interactive CLI and public browser editor, output, pause, step and inspection
Deterministic artifacts, real-kernel regressions, independent literal reference and algorithmic oracles
Auditable host boundary, real development history, complete records and public Site/repository
brainfuckNativeResponsibilities: Source tokenization and unsigned number parsing
Compilation, control-flow patching and code dispatch
Reusable functions, recursion and defining words
Arithmetic, stack and address checks, bulk memory
Indexed records, tombstones, staged/committed views, integrity validation
Graph validation, Dijkstra distances, predecessor/path reconstruction
hostResponsibilities: Generic BF execution and optimization, Wasm packing/compilation
Byte I/O, work limits and process/worker lifecycle
Opaque machine image validation, encoding, hashing and file durability
Editor, forms, emitted-record/path rendering and optional WebMCP discovery
Static asset hosting, build tools, CI and independent test oracles

verification.regressions: 50/50 current tests pass; no known remaining regression
verification.reproducibility: PASS: deterministic regeneration and 50/50 tests in the authoring tree, clean public clone, and Linux CI; see verification.json
verification.boundaryAudit: PASS: 56 classified components and mutation checks; heuristic review gates, not formal proof
verification.selfAudit: PASS within documented scope; sole-agent review, see self-audit.md

knownLimitations: Fixed 256-entry dictionary, 8192-word code, 4096-word heap and 4096-word store
128 records; Dispatch supports 32 nodes and 128 directed roads with weights 1 through 1000
Monotonic allocation and dictionary growth; no reclaiming allocator
Single execution stream; no process isolation, sockets, user permissions or multitasking
Generated kernel uses substantial Python bootstrap tooling; not self-hosting or 8-bit portable
tx-commit is guest commit; explicit image save/export provides external durability
Images are integrity-checked but not authenticated or encrypted; same kernel/mode required
Sole-agent review, finite tests and heuristic audit do not constitute independent proof
A deliberately full collision chain took about 35 to 37 seconds and multiple bounded runs; no fast worst-case claim
finalAssessment: PASS for the bounded Build 001 capability bar: a programmable native compiler/runtime with reusable software, transactional indexed data, serializable continuation, interaction, inspection and dynamic graph computation. Limitations and failed attempts are explicit. Publication identity is recorded separately in publication.json.

nextFrontier.title: Native source workspace with a reclaiming module loader
nextFrontier.reason: Store editable source and named modules inside the constrained system, recompile from native storage and reclaim replaced code/data without invalidating live references; substantially harder state ownership and compatibility than whole-machine snapshots.

publication.state: Deployment identity and anonymous verification are appended after the exact source is published.

repairDebugCycles.method: Grouped corrective engineering episodes, excluding ordinary feature authoring, authentication diagnosis and a corrected test fixture; not a count of every edit or tool failure.
episodes: Hash dictionary after compilation work limit
Paged native code after slow linear dispatch
Indexed format-2 store after full-capacity failure
Atomic byte input and precise work-budget validation
Worker pause, output and no-progress limits plus visible error handling
Rejected universal binary division and retained adaptive native division
Single-pass insertion probing and bounded image continuation for hostile collisions

architectureMigrations: Linear dictionary to native chained hash lookup
Flat code access to native paged program counters
Linear record handling to open-addressed format-2 store; unpublished development images retained their own library
